newsitem.title: USA: Tropical storm Ana heading away from U.S. coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm Ana heading away from U.S. coast.

text.p: A weather system spinning off the southeastern U.S. coast remained a tropical storm Wednesday, but forecasters said it posed no threat to U.S. Independence Day barbecues as it headed away from the shore.

At 5:00 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT), Tropical Storm Ana's centre was near latitude 33.1 north and longitude 70.2 west, or about 350 miles east-southeast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, the National Hurricane Centre said.

The storm was moving northeast, and away from the U.S. coast, at a speed of near 13 mph. Forecasters said that motion was expected to continue through Wednesday with a gradual increase in forward speed.
Maximum sustained winds had decreased to 40 mph, making Ana barely a tropical storm. The forecasters said it could be over cooler waters and become extra-tropical before Saturday.
Ana is the first tropical storm of the June-November Atlantic hurricane season.
